types.name: qttune_frame_t
types.decl:
typedef struct qttune_frame {
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* Microseconds since SESSION START (producer's
                                 steady clock, monotonic per channel) */
    uint32_t arbitration_id;  /* CAN identifier: <= 0x7FF standard, up to
                                 0x1FFFFFFF when FLAG_EXTENDED set */
    uint16_t channel_id;      /* Bus/channel index only — never multiplexes
                                 an arbitration ID */
    uint16_t data_length;     /* Bytes used in data[]: 0..64 */
    uint8_t  data[64];        /* Classic CAN (8) .. CAN-FD (64) payload */
    uint32_t flags;           /* QTTUNE_FRAME_FLAG_* bitmask */
    uint32_t reserved;        /* Producers MUST leave zero; ABI growth space */
} qttune_frame_t;
types.doc: Frame structure — POD only, no pointers. Layout is pinned by the assertions below: sizeof == 88 with ZERO hidden padding on every supported platform (the old struct was also 88 bytes, but 7 of them were accidental tail padding). ABI breaking change: is_extended/rsvd are GONE, replaced by flags/reserved; data_length is now uint16_t; arbitration_id separates CAN identity from channel index. Same-size, better geometry.

types.name: qttune_transport_ops_t
types.doc: Transport abstraction (internal): sessions own a transport instance polymorphically. ops is a pointer to static, immutable vtable storage owned by the transport implementation TU; impl is the implementation's private state. Both start() and detach() are invoked by the session, never by transports themselves — no re-entry into session lifecycle. Contract: - start(): called from qttune_session_start. Must be idempotent (second call on a running transport returns QT_OK). - detach(): called exactly once from qttune_session_close, AFTER the closed flag is set. Must stop any worker threads and free impl + the qttune_transport wrapper itself. May not touch session afterwards.

types.doc: ---- The message struct (J2534-1 v04.04, VERIFIED) ---- FIX 2026-10-15: field order was Timestamp, ExtraDataIndex, DataSize — the last two were SWAPPED vs. the spec. All in-tree access is by field name and every consumer compiles from this header, so the fix is invisible to the test suite by construction; against a real vendor DLL the old order read ExtraDataIndex as DataSize (equal values on unpadded single frames — silent corruption only on padded/multiframe, and wrong tx lengths for Part 4 writes).

types.doc: Response: GROWS downward-compatibly (new fields appended). Old child + new parent fails the pipe length check loudly; never silent garbage. Field semantics by opcode: handle_or_channel: device_id (OPEN), channel (CONNECT/WRITE), filter_id (START_FILTER) aux:               messages actually written (WRITE) — vendors may partially write; the caller decides if partial is an error data/data_len:     GET_CONFIG write-back (updated flattened SCONFIG pairs), or READ_VBATT's 4-byte result

types.name: qttune_sur_ring_slot_t
types.doc: Data-plane ring slot — PASSTHRU_MSG normalized to frame-sized payload. NOTE: 64-byte cap means ISO 15765 multiframe (up to 4128) must be REASSEMBLED surrogate-side before push — Part 3 work, documented.

types.name: qttune_sur_ring_t
types.doc: SPSC ring: producer (surrogate read pump) owns HEAD, consumer (app) owns TAIL. Both monotonic; occupancy = head - tail; slot index = pos & (SIZE-1). Correct on x86/x64 strong memory models (store order preserved); this is a Win32 pair by construction — do not port to weakly-ordered targets without adding barriers.

types.name: qttune_pid_scheduler
types.doc: Round-robin PID scheduler (ADR-0013 slice 2). Fixed capacity, no allocation, owned exclusively by the transport worker thread — single-threaded by construction, so no synchronization inside. PID derivation rule (the contract binding defs to this scheduler): a def drives scheduling iff it carries a 2-byte mux key at payload offset 0. WIRE GRAMMAR (N1 fix, 2026-10-19): on an ISO 15765 channel the ADAPTER owns ISO-TP framing — PassThruWriteMsgs data is [4-byte ID BE][01][PID] (no PCI byte; padding is the ISO15765_FRAME_PAD TxFlag) and a response arrives as [41][PID][A][B]... after the transport strips the 4-byte address header. So the mux pair sits at offset 0 and the PID to REQUEST is the key's LOW byte — the echo grammar guarantees that correspondence. Non-mux defs (raw/mock sets) never enroll; the scheduler simply comes up empty and the worker stays in legacy poll mode. Validators enforce the shape at registration time; from_set() re-checks defensively anyway — it's cheap.
